title: Argument that surveillance trends justify alarm

title: Analogy comparing dress codes across cultures
why: Political argument comparing Afghan face coverings with Western modesty norms; opinion rather than informative content.

title: Angry proposal to boycott US services
why: Emotional political rant proposing boycotts and expulsions; no informative content.

title: Opinion on Facebook entering dating
why: Speculative opinion about a product launch and its safety benefits; no firm technical or expert knowledge conveyed.

title: How timeshare sales pitches hide the real loan cost
why: Pitches quote pennies a day; the real cost is a 12-13 percent APR loan on a roughly $40k purchase.

title: Why VC blog posts reflect the author's incentives
why: VCs earn from rare big exits and frequent bailouts, so public arguments often serve their deal-flow goals.

title: Question on why consoles are so similar now
why: Casual question and speculation about identical console hardware; asks rather than explains.

title: Key travel and bottoming out can cause RSI
why: Switch stop hardness and travel matter for RSI; bottoming out at high typing speed adds strain beyond the tactile bump.

title: Mutable IOArray updates in Haskell, with working code
why: Haskell has mutable arrays via Data.Array.IO; readArray and writeArray give ordinary in-place mutation in IO.

title: Throwaway allegations against a named engineer
why: Unverified personal accusations and gossip about coworkers; no technical or instructive content.

title: Analysis of foreign governments' stances on Snowden
why: Geopolitical commentary on diplomatic positions about one individual; opinion and speculation, not technical knowledge.

title: Argument for natural origin of Omicron
why: Contested origin debate built on one case study and rhetoric; a position statement rather than settled, instructive content.

title: Outrage over Silk Road operator's bounty
why: Moral outrage about a court case and quoted messages; no lesson beyond condemnation.

title: Personal take on whether old internet persists
why: Subjective view that old online communities still exist; opinion without technical substance.

title: Complaint about proprietary math software licensing
why: Opinion on open source versus proprietary licensing for developers; advocacy, not explanation.

title: Payment accounting is harder than payment processing
why: Reconciling fees, refunds, chargebacks and VAT across providers takes months; the charge API is the easy part.

title: Personal story about a spider signaling for help
why: Charming anecdote about spider behavior; the observation is interesting but offers no general lesson.

title: Personal account of a firing dispute at Amazon
why: Employment grievance story with personal conflict; no transferable technical or practical lesson.

title: Political argument about US responsibility in Ukraine
why: Geopolitical opinion with a reading list; contested political argument rather than verifiable instruction.

title: Personal reflection on vegetarianism and cuisines
why: Personal dietary reflection; pleasant but not a substantive explanation a technical reader would learn from.

title: V8 isolates need OS sandboxing, processes add limits
why: Isolates in one process give weak isolation; separate processes with cgroups, namespaces or VMs give stronger limits.

title: Appeal to pilot authority on aircraft stability
why: Relies on claims from an unnamed expert and links; the text cuts off before any concrete explanation of MCAS.

title: Defense of Stallman and critique of media coverage
why: Partisan controversy commentary about a public figure; argument rather than instructive content.

title: Skeptical take on SSD gaming hype
why: Opinion that fast storage will not change gaming much; persuasive rhetoric without concrete technical analysis.

title: Proposal for hot-swappable car battery service
why: Business idea for swappable batteries; a proposal and speculation rather than verified knowledge.

title: Argument that citizens are responsible for corruption
why: Political opinion about democracy and anti-corruption bills; contested argument without concrete evidence.

title: Speculation about how the tablet market plays out
why: Prediction about HP, Apple and Android tablets; speculative forecast without expert grounding.

title: Why an early startup should stay on AWS
why: Managing storage at scale distracts early teams; migrating off cloud early has high opportunity cost and delayed payback.

title: Why a game server chose Rust and data-oriented ECS
why: Memory safety cut debugging time, and cache-coherent ECS design let servers handle hundreds of players and millions of entities.

title: Tight campaigns and negative keywords make ads profitable
why: Match landing pages to exact keywords, add negatives every few days, and track sales back to cut wasteful clicks.

title: Why PHP succeeded as a templating language
why: PHP serves non-programmer themers who edit HTML, a user group most frameworks ignore; that explains its popularity.

title: Adaptability beats stockpiles in disaster survival
why: Plans fail; resilience, knowing when to stay put or move, and minimal kit matter more than stockpiles and weapons.

title: Flawed estimate of molecular interactions for abiogenesis
why: Author admits the calculation is broken; the arithmetic does not support any conclusion about how likely life is.

title: Review of Google Contributor ad removal
why: Subjective product review; it notes blank ad blocks and continued tracking, but is a consumer opinion.

title: Personal account of a police incident
why: Personal grievance about police and a hospital; a story of mistreatment without a transferable lesson.

title: The hard part of management is unpopular decisions
why: Feel-good principles are easy; real management means saying no, making unpopular calls and resolving long-running team conflict.

title: Wishlist for paid services with data control
why: Consumer complaint listing demands for privacy and data export; expresses frustration rather than teaching anything.

title: Review of online coding course platforms
why: Personal learning-platform comparison and frustrations; subjective experience rather than a general technical lesson.

title: Question about a single-cable portable desktop
why: Asks for product recommendations and describes a need; a question rather than an explanation.

title: Limiting cloud lock-in by using few services
why: Using only compute, DNS and object storage keeps a company able to move to its own datacenter in about a week.

title: Opinion on loss-leader pricing and customer trust
why: Business opinion that price changes anger users; reasonable but argumentative, with no firm evidence or method.

title: Agriculture uses most California water, not lawns
why: Residential outdoor watering is tiny next to agriculture, over 80 percent of state water use, so conservation targets the wrong place.

title: Question about confusing cloud compute options
why: Asks why there are so many compute instance families and pricing tiers; a question, not an explanation.

title: The practical problems that break CSV data exchange
why: Encoding is unknowable, Excel mangles numbers and dates, BOMs vary, and most CSV libraries fail the spec in different ways.

title: Personal account of an iPhone repair dispute
why: Customer complaint about a repair quote and support experience; a story without a general technical lesson.

title: Argument about distrust of intellectuals and scientists
why: Sweeping cultural and political argument about scientists and intellectuals; contested opinion, not instructive content.

title: Critique of absolute honesty as life advice
why: Argues with a self-help article using a hypothetical; opinion about social dynamics rather than verifiable knowledge.

title: Why Symbian and MeeGo were not viable for Nokia
why: MeeGo was far from shippable by 2010, and Symbian's UI made basic search-as-you-type a multi-team engineering problem.

title: Story of a performance fix and workplace retaliation
why: Personal workplace story with a notable speedup, but the main content is a grievance and a dramatic exit.

title: Why hands-free speech UX fights headset protocols
why: Standard AT voice commands need a hold-then-beep flow; hold-to-talk needs AVRCP hacks, and SCO packet loss hurts accuracy.

title: Proposal for citizens to record public life
why: Speculative argument for private recording and its benefits; asks an open question rather than teaching a fact.

title: Personal story of running a chat forum
why: Experience of moderating abuse and shutting down a forum; sobering, but a personal narrative without a technical lesson.

title: Benefit cliffs act like a 100 percent marginal tax
why: Basic income is cheaper and avoids cliffs where a job wipes out benefits; fairness intuitions explain resistance.

title: Frustration with agile teams that ignore customers
why: Career complaint about roadmaps and distance from customers; opinion and venting rather than a method.

title: Argument against platform bans on vaccine content
why: Political free speech argument about vaccines and lab leaks; contested opinion without evidence.

title: Interviewer's theory on why brainteasers are used
why: Speculative pet theory about interviewers' motives; personal opinion rather than instructive content.

title: Unvalidated idea for character-level language model
why: Early-stage research idea with no results; the author admits the method is untested.

title: Dropbox product manager responds to account controversy
why: Company statement describing policy changes; corporate response rather than a technical explanation.

title: Argument that hoarding causes artificial scarcity
why: Political argument about price gouging laws during shortages; opinion about ethics and markets.

title: Brainstorm of startup ideas
why: List of product ideas such as a mesh ISP and news recommendation; brainstorming with no explanation.

title: Argument that Congress should pass privacy law
why: Policy argument about FCC authority and privacy; contested legal opinion rather than settled, teachable content.

title: Comparison of two NSA surveillance bills
why: Political commentary on pending bills; informative about the bills but focused on advocacy and the legislative fight.

title: Venting about broken tech hiring practices
why: Opinion on hiring tests and a tip to decline them; advice is anecdotal and mostly complaint.

title: Angry rant about Internet Explorer 11
why: Emotional browser criticism and grudges; no technical or practical lesson.

title: Personal story about a dropped-call phone
why: Anecdote about a broken phone and call handover; the mechanism is mentioned but the story is mostly personal.

title: Opinion that on-device scanning enables surveillance
why: Speculative political argument about Apple's photo scanning and government use; opinion rather than verified fact.

title: Bitcoin's volatility and thin liquidity explained
why: Daily volume near 20,000 means a 15,000 dollar order could move price 5-10 percent; volatility far exceeds stocks.

title: Idea for a battery-efficient programming terminal
why: Enthusiastic design proposal for a low-power device; an idea and wish list rather than verified expertise.

title: Productivity is an energy problem, not a time problem
why: Hard tasks drain energy, so schedule demanding work for peak energy and recharge rather than fill time.

title: Analysis of Catalan and Spanish nationalism
why: Political commentary on independence and nationalism; contested opinion rather than factual knowledge.

title: Back-of-envelope cost of gravity-based grid storage
why: E=mgh means storing 12 hours of California power by rail cars needs over a billion kilograms, costing far more than pumped hydro.

title: Teaching computational thinking before any code
why: CS Unplugged activities build computational thinking first; block languages feel fake to teens, so teach text code afterwards.

title: A practical take-home test that predicts real skill
why: Ask candidates to build a small real app, then have them self-review it live; self-critique reveals skill better than puzzles.

title: Soviet official's grocery visit exposed system's fragility
why: Yeltsin's reaction to Houston supermarkets shows how seeing abundance abroad undermined Soviet elites' faith in their system.

title: Analysis of a staged NSA keynote at Black Hat
why: Political strategy commentary about a speech and audience reaction; interpretive opinion, not technical content.

title: Speculation that Snapchat will dominate AR
why: Industry prediction and promotion of a company's strategy; speculative opinion from an interested party.

title: Why stack languages struggle with ordinary expressions
why: Stack juggling is harder than writing algebra; a practical language needs local variables even when you think you do not.

title: Personal account of a North Korea tour
why: Travel anecdote comparing tour companies; entertaining but personal, with no general technical lesson.

title: Account of confronting sexist jokes at a talk
why: Personal story about gender bias at a conference; a moral reflection rather than instructive content.

title: Story of an alleged Amazon kickback scheme
why: Narrative about a legal case and whistleblower; allegations and drama rather than technical or practical knowledge.

title: Complaint about Pylance license restrictions
why: Criticism of Microsoft's license terms and motives; advocacy and accusation without technical explanation.

title: Quote from a novel about a navy test
why: Fictional anecdote from Cryptonomicon about an aptitude test; entertaining quotation, not a technical explanation.

title: Moderator explanation of job ad policy
why: Site moderation policy about why job ads are excluded; meta discussion about the forum itself.

title: Moderator explanation of banning and shadowbanning
why: Site moderation note on banning and spam handling; meta discussion about forum administration.

title: Opinion on managing review comments in email
why: Personal workflow preference and an idea for patch-plus-comment formats; opinion and sketch, not a settled practice.

title: Dynamic linking matters for patching, not sharing
why: The key benefit of .so files is swapping library versions without rebuilding closed binaries, not sharing code between programs.

title: Interviewer calibration and referrals matter at Google
why: Raw interview scores are calibrated across interviewers so they mean little alone; a strong internal referral helps more than one answer.

title: Why radiology is a good target for automation
why: Radiologists spend most time at workstations; PACS and DICOM standardize image data, so bottlenecks are data access and adoption.

title: Speculation about semiconductor talent crossing the strait
why: Geopolitical speculation about talent migration and China's chip future; anecdotal and opinion-heavy.

title: Argument that India's poverty reflects land and climate
why: Contested argument about climate, property rights and corruption in India; opinion rather than settled evidence.

title: Commentary on Johnson and political narrative
why: Essayistic political commentary about UK leadership and narrative power; opinion, not instructive content.

title: Earthquake deaths depend on timing: tide, night, season
why: A large quake at high tide, at night or in winter causes far more deaths, so timing matters as much as magnitude.

title: Racket's documentation and language-building strengths
why: Racket's Scribble docs far outclass Common Lisp's, and Racket's language-building tools shine for domain-specific languages.

title: Definition of an operating system versus distribution
why: An OS is software that provides and limits hardware access; distributions bundle utilities, so naming follows who wrote what.

title: Rant about a professor's handling of cheating
why: Angry criticism of a professor and the course; personal grievance and opinion rather than instructive content.

title: Opinion that performance reviews are unnecessary
why: Personal career story and management preference; opinion about hiring for self-direction, not a verifiable method.

title: Comparison of dystopian novels 1984 and Brave New World
why: Literary and political comparison of two novels; interpretive opinion about fictional societies.

title: Critique of crypto hype against social goals

title: Complaint about Facebook feed filled with non-friend content
why: User experience complaint describing shrinking original posts from friends; anecdotal observation without a transferable lesson.

title: Why non-bingeable spaced learning builds lasting skill
why: Exponential review intervals and daily stopping force retention; the design aims at durable learning rather than cramming.
